evidence: Migration 20260988 adds emergency_contact_add_by_identifier: a contact can be added by mobile number, email or username, resolved inside a SECURITY DEFINER function — the same route team access uses (grant_business_access), so there is still no directory to browse. The screen asks for the identifier first and keeps the chat-based picker below it. Forced-rollback tested on staging: before 42883; after, adding by phone and by username both work, yourself is refused (CANNOT_ADD_YOURSELF) and an unknown number gives USER_NOT_FOUND.

listContacts throws on a query error instead of returning [], so a network or auth blip shows the error state with a retry rather than 'No emergency contacts' — the most alarming possible lie on this screen.

Migration 20260988 caps the list at 10, both in the add function and in a BEFORE INSERT trigger covering the older chat-based path, so start_live_share's per-contact inserts stay bounded. Verified on staging with throwaway users: the 11th add fails with TOO_MANY_CONTACTS and the list stays at 10.
The screen reads through useQueryWithRealtime on emergency_contacts filtered to owner_user_id=eq.<uid>, so a change made on another device lands here.
Candidate Add buttons are 44px minimum with an accessible name ('Add <name> as an emergency contact'), and the identifier field has a label and a 44px Add button.

Migration 20260987: revoke_live_share_recipient ends the live_shares row once its last recipient is gone. Forced-rollback tested on staging: before, the share stayed ACTIVE after both recipients were revoked (broadcasting a GPS fix every 12 seconds to nobody); after, it ends.
locationService.sharedByMe excludes grants whose expires_at has passed, so 'Currently sharing with' shows only live ones.

Every location_share_grants subscription (LocationSettings' three queries and Home's pending-requests query) filters on owner_user_id=eq.<uid>, so one person's grant no longer wakes every connected client.
LiveShareBanner offsets by the safe-area inset (top: calc(8px + var(--safe-area-top, env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)))), so it clears a notch or punch-hole.

LiveLocationCard tears the Leaflet map down on unmount, not only when the share ends, so leaving the screen mid-share (or a StrictMode double-mount) no longer leaves the container attached and the next mount doesn't throw 'Map container is already initialized'.
